goals: Define the Renaissance and say where and when it began
Explain how the capture of Constantinople in 1453 and the decline of feudalism helped it
Explain how trade, patrons, the spirit of enquiry and the printing press spread new ideas
Place the main events on a time line

slides.heading: The Renaissance: meaning and causes
slides.body_md: Part 1 — what the Renaissance was, and why it began.

visual.alt: Route map of Part 1: the meaning of the Renaissance and where it began, then the capture of Constantinople, feudalism and trade, then the spirit of enquiry and the printing press
visual.caption: Part 1 at a glance

slides.narration: In this part we learn what the word Renaissance means and where it began. Then we study the causes. These are the capture of Constantinople, the decline of feudalism, new trade routes and wealth, the spirit of enquiry, and the printing press.

slides.heading: What is the Renaissance?
bullets: A **French word** meaning **rebirth**.
A revival of interest in **classical Greek and Roman learning**.
Together with **new ideas** in art, literature and science.
Lasted about the **14th to the 16th century**.

rows: Interest in classical Greek and Roman learning
New ideas in art, literature and science

visual.alt: Table about the Renaissance: a French word meaning rebirth, a revival of interest in classical Greek and Roman learning together with new ideas in art, literature and science, lasting about the 14th to 16th century

slides.narration: Renaissance is a French word that means rebirth. It was a revival of interest in the learning of ancient Greece and Rome. It also brought new ideas in art, literature and science. The age lasted from about the fourteenth to the sixteenth century.

slides.narration: This web shows six causes. The capture of Constantinople, the decline of feudalism, new trade routes, wealthy patrons, the spirit of enquiry and the printing press all fed the Renaissance. They are not in order of importance. They worked together and strengthened one another.

slides.heading: Where and when it began
bullets: It began in **Italy**, in the city of **Florence**.
It then **spread across Europe**.
It lasted about the **14th to 16th century**.

nodes.label: Spreads to France, Germany, England and more

visual.alt: Flow: the Renaissance begins in Italy in the city of Florence, spreads across Europe, and lasts about the 14th to the 16th century
visual.caption: Where and when.

slides.narration: The Renaissance began in Italy, in the city of Florence. From there it spread across Europe. It lasted from about the fourteenth to the sixteenth century, so we use the word about with these dates.

slides.heading: The capture of Constantinople, 1453
bullets: The **Ottoman Turks** took the city in **1453**.
It was the capital of the **Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire**.
Two results: one for **learning**, one for **trade**.

rows: Capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire
Two results, one for learning and one for trade

visual.alt: Table about the capture of Constantinople: taken by the Ottoman Turks in 1453, the capital of the Eastern Roman or Byzantine Empire, with two results one for learning and one for trade

slides.narration: In fourteen fifty three the Ottoman Turks took Constantinople. It was the capital of the Eastern Roman empire, also called the Byzantine empire. The event had two important results, one for learning and one for trade.

slides.heading: Two results of 1453

nodes.label: Greek scholars carry manuscripts to Italy

visual.alt: Flow: the Ottoman Turks take Constantinople in 1453, Greek scholars carry manuscripts to Italy, and the study of classical texts grows
visual.caption: Effect on learning.

slides.narration: First, Greek scholars moved to Italy and carried manuscripts with them. This encouraged the study of classical texts. Second, trade routes to the East were disrupted, which encouraged Europeans to search for new sea routes. The next slide shows the second result.

slides.heading: The search for new sea routes

nodes.label: Routes to the East are disrupted
Europeans want other ways to Asia

visual.alt: Flow: routes to the East are disrupted, Europeans want other ways to Asia, and a search for new sea routes begins
visual.caption: Effect on trade.

slides.narration: When the old routes to the East became hard to use, Europeans wanted other ways to reach Asia. This pushed them to search for new sea routes, and so it is a link between the Renaissance and the voyages of discovery.

slides.heading: The decline of feudalism
bullets: The **Crusades** weakened many feudal lords.
The **Black Death** (about 1347 to 1351) caused **labour shortages**; peasants could demand **wages**.
**Towns, trade and a money economy** grew; a **rich middle class** emerged.
**Gunpowder and cannon** made castles and knights less important.
**Kings grew stronger.**

rows: Labour shortage; peasants could demand wages
Growth of towns, trade and a money economy
Castles and knights became less important

visual.alt: Table of developments and their effect on feudalism: the Crusades weakened lords, the Black Death caused labour shortages and wage demands, towns and trade created a rich middle class, cannon made castles less important, and kings grew stronger

slides.narration: Feudalism declined slowly, for many reasons. The Crusades weakened many lords. The Black Death, about thirteen forty seven to thirteen fifty one, left few workers, so peasants could demand wages. Towns, trade and money grew, and a rich middle class appeared. Cannon made castles less useful, and kings grew stronger.

slides.heading: From weak lords to strong kings

nodes.label: Lords weakened; peasants gain bargaining power
Towns, trade and a middle class grow

visual.alt: Flow: lords weakened and peasants gain bargaining power, towns trade and a middle class grow, and kings grow stronger
visual.caption: The decline of feudalism.

slides.narration: Follow the chain. As lords grew weaker, peasants gained bargaining power. Towns and trade grew, and a middle class became richer. At the same time kings grew stronger. This changed society and made room for new ideas.

slides.heading: Trade and wealth
bullets: **Venice and Genoa**: Italian city-states made rich by trade.
Towns, banks and a **rich middle class** grew.
Voyages were **linked consequences**: **Columbus, 1492**; **Vasco da Gama, Calicut, 1498**.

rows: Italian city-states made rich by trade with the East
Towns, banks and a rich middle class
Columbus 1492; Vasco da Gama reached Calicut 1498

visual.alt: Table about trade and wealth: Venice and Genoa were Italian city-states made rich by trade with the East, with towns, banks and a middle class as a result, and voyages as linked consequences, Columbus in 1492 and Vasco da Gama at Calicut in 1498

slides.narration: Italian city-states such as Venice and Genoa became rich from trade. Towns, banks and a rich middle class grew. The voyages of Columbus in fourteen ninety two and of Vasco da Gama to Calicut in fourteen ninety eight were linked consequences of the search for new routes.

slides.heading: Patrons and voyagers
bullets: The **Medici of Florence** were wealthy **patrons**.
They supported **artists and scholars**.
**Columbus** crossed the Atlantic; **Vasco da Gama** reached **Calicut**.

rows: Wealthy patrons who supported artists and scholars
Reached Calicut in India by sea

visual.alt: Table: the Medici of Florence were wealthy patrons who supported artists and scholars, Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492, and Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498

slides.narration: Wealthy patrons paid for art and learning. The best known are the Medici of Florence, who supported artists and scholars. Columbus crossed the Atlantic, and Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in India by sea.

slides.heading: The spirit of enquiry and humanism
bullets: **Questioning** of tradition and authority.
Reliance on **reason, observation and experiment**.
**Humanism**: interest in human life and abilities.
**Petrarch** is often called the **father of humanism**.

rows: Interest in human life and abilities
Often called the father of humanism

visual.alt: Table: the spirit of enquiry is questioning tradition and authority, its method is reason observation and experiment, humanism is interest in human life and abilities, and Petrarch is often called the father of humanism

slides.narration: People began to question tradition and authority. They relied on reason, observation and experiment. Humanism was an interest in human life and abilities. The Italian writer Petrarch is often called the father of humanism.

sections.heading: 1. Meaning of the Renaissance
sections.body_md:
- **Renaissance** is a French word meaning **rebirth**. It was a revival of interest in **classical Greek and Roman learning**, together with new ideas in art, literature and science.
- It lasted about the **14th to the 16th century**. It began in **Italy**, in the city of **Florence**, and spread across Europe.
- It was not a sudden change: several causes worked together over many years.

The ideas and writings of ancient Greece and Rome.

sections.heading: 2. Causes: Constantinople and the decline of feudalism
sections.body_md:
- **Capture of Constantinople (1453):** the **Ottoman Turks** took the city, the capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire. Greek scholars moved to **Italy** with manuscripts, which encouraged the study of classical texts. Trade routes to the East were disrupted, which encouraged the search for new sea routes.
- **Decline of feudalism:** the **Crusades** weakened many lords. The **Black Death** (about 1347 to 1351) caused labour shortages, so peasants could demand wages. **Towns, trade and a money economy** grew and a **rich middle class** emerged. **Gunpowder and cannon** made castles and knights less important. **Kings grew stronger.**

key_terms.definition_md: A system in which lords held land and peasants worked it.
A deadly plague that struck Europe about 1347 to 1351.
Townspeople, such as traders, who were neither lords nor peasants.

sections.heading: 3. Causes: trade, patrons and the spirit of enquiry
sections.body_md:
- **Trade:** Italian city-states such as **Venice and Genoa** grew rich from trade with the East. **Patrons** such as the **Medici of Florence** used their wealth to support artists and scholars.
- **Voyages** were linked consequences: **Columbus** crossed the Atlantic in **1492**, and **Vasco da Gama** reached **Calicut** in **1498**.
- **Spirit of enquiry:** people questioned tradition and authority and relied on **reason, observation and experiment**.
- **Humanism** is an interest in human life and abilities. **Petrarch** is often called the **father of humanism**.

sections.heading: 4. Causes: the printing press
sections.body_md:
- **Johannes Gutenberg** of **Mainz** developed printing with **movable metal type** about **1450**. The **Gutenberg Bible** dates to about **1455**.
- **William Caxton** printed in **England** from **1476**.
- **Effects:** books became cheaper and more numerous, literacy spread, and ideas travelled faster across Europe.

key_terms.definition_md: Separate metal letters that can be arranged, inked and reused.
The ability to read and write.

sections.heading: 5. Impact: Leonardo, Shakespeare and Copernicus
sections.body_md:
- **Leonardo da Vinci (1452 to 1519):** painter, scientist and engineer. Works include **The Last Supper** and the **Mona Lisa**. His notebooks hold studies of **anatomy** and designs for **flying machines** and other devices. He is called a **universal man** (Renaissance man).
- **William Shakespeare (1564 to 1616):** English playwright and poet. Plays include **Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet, Julius Caesar** and **The Merchant of Venice**. He wrote **about 37 to 39 plays**, as counts vary, and sonnets. He wrote about **human nature** and enriched the English language.
- **Nicolaus Copernicus (1473 to 1543):** a Polish astronomer who proposed that the **earth and planets move around the sun** (**heliocentric** theory). This challenged the older **earth-centred (geocentric, Ptolemaic)** view. His book was published in **1543** and laid the foundation for later astronomers such as **Galileo** and **Kepler**.

sections.heading: 6. Consequences of the Renaissance
sections.body_md:
- **Humanism:** interest in human life and abilities.
- **Realism in art:** perspective, a study of anatomy and a close look at nature.
- **Growth of science** and the experimental method.
- **Vernacular languages and literature:** Dante wrote in Italian and Chaucer in English, and the printing press helped such books to spread.
- **Strong nation-states:** lords grew weaker and kings stronger.
- A **spirit of enquiry** that encouraged geographical discoveries and, later, the Reformation (the next chapter).

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Writing a date without the word about when it is approximate.
- Giving only one result of the fall of Constantinople; there are two, one for learning and one for trade.
- Confusing Gutenberg (Mainz, about 1450) with Caxton (England, from 1476).
- Saying that Copernicus put the earth at the centre; he put the sun there.
- Listing a painting as a play, or a play as a painting.
- Treating the Renaissance as only about art.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1-mark items: one correct option, name or term.
- 2 marks: two distinct points; 3 marks: three points.
- 10-mark questions in 3 + 3 + 4 parts: one clear point per mark; the last part usually needs a reason, a link or an evaluation.

cards.front_md: What was reborn in the Renaissance?
cards.back_md: Interest in **classical Greek and Roman learning**, with new ideas in art, literature and science.

cards.front_md: When and where did the Renaissance begin?
cards.back_md: About the **14th century**, in **Italy** (Florence); it lasted to about the 16th century.
**Greek scholars** moved to Italy with **manuscripts**; classical study grew.
Trade routes to the East were **disrupted**; search for **new sea routes**.
About **1347 to 1351**; labour shortages, so peasants could **demand wages**.

cards.front_md: How did the Crusades affect feudalism?

cards.back_md: Made **castles and knights** less important; **kings grew stronger**.

cards.front_md: Who emerged as towns and trade grew?

cards.back_md: Wealthy **patrons of Florence** who supported artists and scholars.
**Questioning** of tradition; reliance on **reason, observation and experiment**.
**Cheaper, more numerous** books; **literacy** spread; ideas travelled **faster**.
**The Last Supper** and the **Mona Lisa**; notebooks on **anatomy** and **flying machines**.
A person skilled in **many fields**; Leonardo is the example.
**Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet, Julius Caesar, The Merchant of Venice**; about **37 to 39** plays.
Wrote about **human nature**; **enriched the English language**.
**Copernicus**: the **earth and planets move around the sun**.
Writing in local languages: **Dante** in Italian, **Chaucer** in English.

questions.stem_md: The imagined Rivermead Art Club prints a poster titled "Our Renaissance Week". A visitor asks about the word. Which language does it come from, and what does it mean?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** French, meaning rebirth. Renaissance is a French word meaning rebirth, used for the revival of interest in classical Greek and Roman learning together with new ideas in art, literature and science. Conquest, travel and printing are not what the word means.

questions.stem_md: In an imagined diary from the year 1453, a Greek teacher called Nikos leaves a city that has just fallen to the Ottoman Turks and sails to Italy with a trunk of old manuscripts. How did journeys like his help the Renaissance?

options.text_md: They ended the use of Greek and Latin in Italy
They created the first printing press in Italy
They made Italian merchants stop trading with the East
They brought classical texts and learning to Italy, where scholars studied them with fresh interest

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** They brought classical texts and learning to Italy, where scholars studied them with fresh interest. Greek scholars moving to Italy with manuscripts encouraged the study of classical texts, a central part of the Renaissance. The printing press came from Mainz and was not created by these journeys, and the fall of the city did not end learning of Greek or Latin.

questions.stem_md: An imagined merchant of Seaview, whose family sold spices, writes in 1460: "Since the great city on the Bosphorus changed hands, our old road to the East is hard to use." What was the long-term result in Europe?

options.text_md: The disruption of the land and sea routes to the East encouraged a search for new sea routes
Europe stopped all trade with Asia for four centuries
Merchants moved their goods only by overland caravans through Constantinople
The Ottomans withdrew from the city within a few years

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The disruption of the land and sea routes to the East encouraged a search for new sea routes. The capture of Constantinople in 1453 disrupted the old trade routes to the East, which encouraged the search for new sea routes. Trade did not stop for centuries, caravans could not use the old route freely, and the Ottomans kept the city.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined manor of Oakdene, about 1350, a plague has killed many farm workers. The surviving labourers refuse to work unless the lord pays wages. Which cause of the decline of feudalism does this show?

options.text_md: The invention of the printing press raised the price of grain
The Crusades ended the need for lords
The Black Death caused labour shortages, so peasants could demand wages
The discovery of the sea route to India

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** The Black Death caused labour shortages, so peasants could demand wages. The Black Death (about 1347 to 1351) left too few workers, so peasants could demand wages. Printing, a sea route to India and the end of the Crusades are not what drove this change in the manor.

questions.stem_md: An imagined guide at the ruined castle of Stonehaven says: "Thick walls once kept armies out, but the new iron guns of a royal army broke them in a single week." Which development does she describe?

options.text_md: The rise of the Black Death, which emptied every castle
The founding of new universities by the Medici
Gunpowder and cannon made castles and knights less important, so kings grew stronger

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Gunpowder and cannon made castles and knights less important, so kings grew stronger. Gunpowder and cannon made castle walls and armoured knights less useful, which weakened feudal lords and strengthened kings. The plague, Medici patronage and movable type belong to other developments.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined port of Marenza, a rich cloth trader who is neither a lord nor a peasant buys books and pays an artist to paint his family. Which group in society does he stand for?

options.text_md: A rich middle class that emerged as towns, trade and a money economy grew
A feudal lord with a large estate
A serf tied to the land
A knight serving in a castle

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** A rich middle class that emerged as towns, trade and a money economy grew. Growing towns and trade, and a money economy, produced a rich middle class that could buy books and support art. A lord holds an estate, a serf is tied to the land and a knight serves in a castle, none of which fits a trader.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined notebook of the Hillcrest History Club, four terms need their meanings. Match each term with its meaning.

match_right.text_md: A system in which lords held land and peasants worked it
The ideas and writings of ancient Greece and Rome
A deadly plague of about 1347 to 1351

questions.solution_md: **Key:** (a)–(r), (b)–(p), (c)–(s), (d)–(q). Renaissance means rebirth, feudalism was the system of lords and peasants, the Black Death was the plague of about 1347 to 1351, and classical learning means ancient Greek and Roman knowledge.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The imagined Rivermead Art Club notes that the Renaissance began in Italy, in the city of Florence, and then spread across Europe.
questions.solution_md: **True.** True. The movement began in Florence, in Italy, and spread to the rest of Europe over the 14th to 16th century.

questions.stem_md: True or false? A student of the imagined Pinewood School writes that Constantinople was taken by the Ottoman Turks in the year 1492.
questions.solution_md: **False.** False. The Ottoman Turks took Constantinople in 1453; 1492 is the year of the first voyage of Columbus.

questions.stem_md: The Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople in the year ___.
questions.solution_md: The year was 1453, when Greek scholars began moving to Italy with their manuscripts.

questions.stem_md: The word Renaissance is a French word that means ___.
questions.solution_md: The word means rebirth, because the age revived interest in classical learning.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Black Death helped to weaken feudalism in Europe.

**Reason (R):** The plague left labour in short supply, so surviving peasants could demand wages instead of serving their lords for nothing.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion: the shortage of labour gave peasants bargaining power, which loosened the hold of the lords.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The capture of Constantinople in 1453 made the old routes to the East easier and safer for European traders.

**Reason (R):** The capture disrupted trade routes to the East and encouraged the search for new sea routes.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** The assertion is false, because the routes were disrupted rather than made easier. The reason is true and states what actually happened.

questions.stem_md: At the opening of the imagined Hillcrest Renaissance fair, a guide asks every visitor to define the word. What is the Renaissance, and when did it take place?
questions.solution_md: Meaning as rebirth of classical learning with new ideas; about the 14th to 16th century.

answer.model_answer_md: The Renaissance, a French word for **rebirth**, was a revival of interest in **classical Greek and Roman learning** along with new ideas in art, literature and science. It lasted from about the **14th to the 16th century**.

marking_scheme.step: Revival of classical Greek and Roman learning with new ideas (rebirth)
About the 14th to the 16th century, beginning in Italy

questions.stem_md: Explain two ways in which the fall of Constantinople to the Ottoman Turks in 1453 affected Europe.
questions.solution_md: Scholars and manuscripts reached Italy; trade routes disrupted, leading to a search for sea routes.

answer.model_answer_md: Greek scholars moved to **Italy** with their **manuscripts**, which encouraged the study of classical texts. The city's fall also **disrupted trade routes to the East**, which encouraged Europeans to look for new sea routes.

marking_scheme.step: Greek scholars and manuscripts reach Italy; classical study encouraged
Trade routes disrupted; search for new sea routes

questions.stem_md: An imagined student, Karan, claims that feudalism ended in a single year when one castle fell. Give two reasons why historians describe a gradual decline instead.
questions.solution_md: Many causes over a long time: Crusades, plague, towns, cannon.

answer.model_answer_md: Several causes worked together over many decades: the **Crusades** weakened many lords, the **Black Death** caused labour shortages, and **towns and trade** grew. Later, **cannon** made castles less useful, so no single event ended feudalism.

marking_scheme.step: Two or more causes named, for example Crusades and Black Death
Idea that causes acted gradually together, not in a single year

questions.stem_md: State three developments that led to the decline of feudalism in Europe.
questions.solution_md: Any three: Crusades, Black Death, trade and towns, cannon, stronger kings.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. The **Crusades** weakened many feudal lords.
2. The **Black Death** (about 1347 to 1351) left few workers, which let peasants ask for wages.
3. **Towns, trade and a money economy** grew, and gunpowder and **cannon** made castles and knights less important, so **kings grew stronger**.

marking_scheme.step: Growth of towns and trade, rise of kings or the middle class

questions.stem_md: An imagined exhibition panel at Rivermead lists "1453, a plague of about 1350, a new kind of cannon". Link each of the three to the Renaissance.
questions.solution_md: Constantinople, Black Death, cannon each linked to a Renaissance cause.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **1453**: Greek scholars moved to Italy with manuscripts, so classical study grew.
2. **The plague of about 1350**, the Black Death, caused labour shortages and helped to weaken feudalism.
3. **Cannon** made castles and knights less important, so kings grew stronger and society changed.

marking_scheme.step: Black Death linked to decline of feudalism

questions.stem_md:
The imagined Hillcrest Heritage Society is preparing a wall chart on how the Renaissance began.

(i) What is meant by the Renaissance, and where did it begin? **[3]**
(ii) How did the capture of Constantinople in 1453 help the Renaissance? **[3]**
(iii) Explain how the Black Death and the growth of towns and trade weakened feudalism. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Meaning and place; effects of 1453; Black Death and growth of towns and trade.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) The Renaissance was a **revival of interest in classical Greek and Roman learning** together with new ideas in art, literature and science. The French word means **rebirth**. It began in **Italy**, in the city of **Florence**, and lasted about the 14th to 16th century.

(ii) When the **Ottoman Turks took Constantinople in 1453**, Greek scholars moved to **Italy** with their manuscripts, and this encouraged the study of classical texts. The city's fall also **disrupted the trade routes to the East**, which pushed Europeans to look for new sea routes.

(iii) The **Black Death** (about 1347 to 1351) left too few workers, so peasants could **demand wages** and the lords lost power. At the same time **towns, trade and a money economy** grew, and a **rich middle class** appeared. As a result the old tie between lord and peasant weakened and **kings grew stronger**.

marking_scheme.step: (i) Revival of classical Greek and Roman learning with new ideas (rebirth)
(i) Began in Italy, Florence; about the 14th to 16th century
(ii) Scholars and manuscripts move to Italy
(ii) Trade routes disrupted; search for sea routes
(iii) Black Death: labour shortage and wages
(iii) Towns, trade and money economy; rich middle class

questions.stem_md: An imagined ledger page in the museum of Marenza shows ships arriving with silk, spices and glass. Which pair of Italian city-states became rich through trade in this age?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Venice and Genoa. Venice and Genoa were Italian city-states that grew rich from trade. Mainz is in Germany and Calicut is in India, while London and Paris are not Italian city-states.

questions.stem_md: An imagined exhibition card at the Rivermead Art Club says: "A banking family of Florence paid painters and sculptors and helped scholars to copy old books." Which family does the card describe?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** The Medici. The Medici of Florence were wealthy patrons who supported artists and scholars. Gutenberg was a printer from Mainz, and the Tudors and Habsburgs were royal houses of other lands.

questions.stem_md: A time-line strip prepared by the imagined class of Pinewood School marks the first voyage of Columbus across the Atlantic. In which year does it belong?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** 1492. Columbus made his first voyage in 1492. The year 1453 is the fall of Constantinople, 1498 is when Vasco da Gama reached Calicut, and 1543 is when Copernicus's book appeared.

questions.stem_md: On an imagined map-quiz board in Seaview, a pin is placed on the Indian port that Vasco da Gama reached in 1498 after sailing round Africa. Which port is it?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Calicut. Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498. Mainz and Florence are in Europe, and Constantinople lay on the old route between Europe and Asia.

questions.stem_md: A caption in the imagined Hillcrest library says: "Often called the father of humanism, this Italian poet turned attention to human life and abilities." Which person fits the caption?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Petrarch. Petrarch is often called the father of humanism. Copernicus was an astronomer, Caxton a printer and Vasco da Gama a sea-voyager.

questions.stem_md: At the imagined Pinewood Science Fair, Meera does not accept the claim that heavier stones always fall faster. She drops two stones from the same height and records what she sees. Which Renaissance attitude does she show?

options.text_md: Feudal loyalty to an older authority
A wish to copy old books by hand
Acceptance of whatever an earlier writer had said
The spirit of enquiry: reliance on reason, observation and experiment rather than only on tradition

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The spirit of enquiry: reliance on reason, observation and experiment rather than only on tradition. Testing a claim by observation and experiment is the spirit of enquiry. Obeying old authority, copying by hand and accepting earlier writers unchallenged go against that attitude.

questions.stem_md: A label in the imagined print museum of Valdoro reads: "In the German town of Mainz, about 1450, a goldsmith began printing with movable metal type." Whose work does it describe?

questions.solution_md: Humanism and realism; science and vernacular literature; nation-states and discoveries.

answer.model_answer_md:

(iii) As **feudal lords weakened**, **kings grew stronger** and **nation-states** developed, helped by taxes from the middle class and by cannon. The **spirit of enquiry** also **encouraged geographical discoveries**, such as the voyages of Columbus and Vasco da Gama, and later the Reformation.
